The atmosphere shifts from the "vuqxw¡t 'ks"k" (carefree laughter) of a child waiting for his father to the "okrkoj.k vkSj jkr&fnu osQ dke osQ cks> osQ dkj.k" (mechanical routine of daily work) of an adult perpetuating the system. A wrong answer calling it "just a flashback structure" fails to see how the recurring setting acts as a measuring rod for moral erosion.

questions.q: Create a 4-sentence atmospheric description of the village path (xk¡o) at dusk that captures the dual mood of childhood freedom and caste surveillance present in the text, using at least three sensory details (sound, smell, touch, sight).
questions.a: A strong answer: "Dust rises from the village path like smoke as eksgu's bare feet kick up the day's heat, the scent of drying dung cakes mixing with marigold from the temple yard. Somewhere a flute plays a fragment of a wedding song, but the sound fractures when the headman's bicycle bell cuts through - a sharp, metallic reminder of who owns the road. The banyan tree's shadow stretches long, offering coolness that feels like permission, yet its trunk bears the carved initials of generations who passed this way only to return as their fathers' shadows. The air tastes of both mango blossoms and the iron tang of the well-water drawn by hands that never touch the bucket." A poor answer listing only pleasant sensory details ("birds singing, cool breeze, pretty flowers") reveals the student cannot hold the story's central tension: that every space of beauty in this village is also a space of caste inscription.
